Commentary.Commentary: Over and out - That brings us to the end of this one-sided contest, with South Africa Women cruising to a 2-0 lead and now eyeing a series-clinching win in the next game. India Women, meanwhile, must win to stay alive in the series. The action now shifts to the Wanderers Stadium in Johannesburg for the third match on 22nd April, Wednesday, starting at 9.30 pm IST (4 pm GMT). Do join us early for all the build-up. Until then, cheers and goodbye!

The victorious skipper of South Africa Women - Laura Wolvaardt says it was pretty good in all three departments. Adds that after the start India had, the bowling unit did well to drag things back. Shares that they have been struggling to execute their bowling in the past few series, but she is happy with how they have handled it in two games so far. Laura reckons there is excitement to win the series, but they'll see the conditions first, expects India to come hard, but they will be ready for the next game.

The captain of India Women - Harmanpreet Kaur says that they were not able to contribute the way they wanted with the bat. Adds that the last 10 overs, they did not bat well and will need to think about how to improve in the remaining three games. Kaur mentions that the Powerplay bowling is also not going their way, but they need to stay together as a team. Says that at the death, if you are not able to hit the shots, strike rotation becomes very important. On Shafali Verma, Karu says that she has been a great talent for them, attacking and scoring runs in the Powerplay and hopefully she continues to do that. Ends by saying that now they are going to a new venue, but the key will be to keep a positive approach and stick together.

PLAYER OF THE MATCH - Chloe Tryon wins the award for her excellent bowling, finishing with figures of 3/22. She says it was nice to do it in front of friends and family, but more importantly, for South Africa. Tryon mentions that Keshav Maharaj has been with them for the past few days and has helped them a lot. He helped her to stick to the basics and change a little bit of her technical game.
Presentation Time...

No answers to Proteas' charge - There isn't much to talk about India's bowling effort. They were a few runs short, but never looked like building any pressure on the hosts. A few fielding lapses and dropped chances didn't help either, while the bowlers were largely inconsistent and had no answers to the Proteas' onslaught. Shreyanka Patil was the only real bright spot with a couple of wickets, but it was too little too late, leaving India with plenty to think about.

India Women lose the plot - Earlier in the game, India Women once again posted a slightly under-par total, despite Shafali Verma marking her 100th WT20I with a fine half-century and Anushka Sharma chipping in on debut. The innings fell away badly as they lost their last eight wickets for just 48 runs. Chloe Tryon led the charge for South Africa Women with 3/22, while Tumi Sekhukhune also picked up three wickets, with Nadine de Klerk and Nonkululeko Mlaba taking one each to cap off a strong bowling effort.

The hosts cruise home - South Africa Women got off to a flying start, led by skipper Laura Wolvaardt's aggression. Sune Luus began cautiously but shifted gears at the right time, and the pair never looked back. They raced to 66 in the Powerplay, equalling their best in the format, and stitched a 106-run opening stand with both bringing up well-made fifties to break the back of the chase. Though neither stayed till the end, they had already set the platform, allowing Tazmin Brits and Annerie Dercksen to finish the job comfortably with just under three overs to spare.

South Africa Women in command - South Africa Women have delivered another strong performance in their own backyard, taking a 2-0 lead in the series and, despite a few flaws, have looked the better side overall in both games. India Women have had their moments but failed to capitalize, and now find themselves in a do-or-die situation.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Nice use of the feet! Flighted, full and around off. Laura Wolvaardt comes down the track, strethes out in front and thumps it past the bowler to the long off fence for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Shreyanka Patil to Laura Wolvaardt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Dragged back and outside off, Sune Luus cuts it away towards point, where the fielder gets a good hand on it. Just a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Shreyanka Patil to Sune Luus, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Slows it up, shortish and on off, turns in sharply, Sune Luus stabs it out to short cover.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Shreyanka Patil to Sune Luus, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: WIDE! Flatter, short but turning down the leg side, Sune Luus fails to paddle it away. Wided.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Shreyanka Patil to Sune Luus, Wide!

Commentary.Commentary: Shreyanka Patil begins with a floater, short and on off, Sune Luus stays back and defends it.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Shreyanka Patil to Sune Luus, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shreyanka Patil bowls now.
Short in length, outside off. Sune Luus punches it away through point for a single. Good start by South Africa Women.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Kranti Gaud to Sune Luus, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Overthrow! Length ball, outside off. Luss slaps it to point for a single. Harmanpreet Kaur throws to the keeper, who fails to stop and it rolls away for another run.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Kranti Gaud to Sune Luus, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Gets the stumps into play as Gaud bowls it full. Laura Wolvaardt drills it to mid on for a quick single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Kranti Gaud to Laura Wolvaardt, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Slashed and slashed hard. Short of a good length and wide outside off. Laura Wolvaardt frees her arms and hammers it though point for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Kranti Gaud to Laura Wolvaardt, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: South Africa Women are underway! Bangs it short and on middle. Laura Wolvaardt picks the length and pulls it hard to deep square leg. The fielder runs to her left, dives and does well to keep the ball away from the ropes. Two runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Kranti Gaud to Laura Wolvaardt, 2 runs.

Commentary.Commentary: Kranti Gaud begins with a fuller delivery on middle. Laura Wolvaardt clips it to square leg.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Kranti Gaud to Laura Wolvaardt, No run.
